reference.title: help-contexts.yaml reference
reference.shortdesc: Maps each app's routes to context keys, so an app can open help by sending its current path, and sets the key to use when nothing more specific matches.

section.title: Format
section.p: The file lives at the docs root. Part of this site's own file:
section.codeblock: apps: opend-console: default: overview routes: /: overview /tenants: tenants /tenants/:tenant: tenants.detail /tenants/:tenant/**: tenants.detail /billing/**: billing /editor/**: editor /editor/:repo/conflicts: editor.conflicts

property.propdesc: One entry per app, named as in resourceid appname and in the widget's app option. Letters, digits, _ and -.
Optional. The key used when the requested key, and every parent of it, has nothing this reader can see.
Route pattern to key, in any order. Optional.

strow.stentry: zero or more segments; last segment only

ul.li: Query strings, fragments, empty segments and trailing slashes in the path are ignored, and percent-encoded segments are decoded, so /Tenants/acme/?tab=users matches /tenants/:tenant.
A segment containing *, :, ? or # other than as above is invalid, and so is ** before the last segment. Both are invalid-help-contexts errors.

section.title: Which route wins
section.p: When several patterns match a path, the most specific wins:

ol.li: the one with more literal segments;
then the one earlier in the file.

section.p: So for /editor/docs/conflicts, /editor/:repo/conflicts (two literals) beats /editor/** (one literal). For /tenants/acme, /tenants/:tenant beats /tenants/:tenant/**, which has the same literals but a **.

section.title: Checks
section.p: Every route and default must name a key that some topic declares with resourceid, or a key with such a parent: tenants.detail is fine while only tenants exists. Anything else is an unknown-context error. A path that matches no route opens the default.
